chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Mansur ibn Hazim from Ibn Abi Yafur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the coating (of impurity) exceeds one-third, it is forbidden."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when impurity covers more than one-third of a surface?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the threshold for *kathrah* (abundance) of impurity on surfaces, establishing that exceeding one-third renders the area ritually impure (*najis*) and thus invalid for prayer (*salah*) unless purified. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor impurity does not invalidate prayer, but once it surpasses this specific proportion, it becomes a significant barrier to ritual validity, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of 'excess' or the Ja'fari view of 'spread'.
